title: Why we’re investing in Dr. Max’s

insights.claim: Collab Fund frames the current venture market as saturated with frothy AI bets and is deliberately allocating into a physician-founded natural personal-care brand as a differentiated, non-AI position.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: Signals that at least some venture allocators see better risk-adjusted entry points in unglamorous consumer brands than in AI valuations — watch for rotation of early-stage capital toward consumer staples-adjacent startups.
insights.quote: In a market saturated with frothy AI bets, we believe our investment in the paradoxical Dr. Max Goldstein, a practicing family physician and a Mendocino farmer, is just what the doctor ordered.
insights.locator: In a market saturated with frothy AI bets

themes.theme: Organic traction as the diligence signal

insights.claim: Dr. Max's became the top-selling brand in children's body care at Erewhon on under $10,000 of total marketing spend, an efficiency data point the investors treat as proof of genuine product-market fit.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: Near-zero customer acquisition cost is the key underwriting metric in DTC consumer right now; benchmark other consumer bets against this marketing-spend-to-category-leadership ratio.
insights.quote: With less than $10k of marketing spend, Dr. Max’s is already the top selling brand in children’s body care in Erewhon.
insights.locator: With less than $10k of marketing spend

insights.claim: The investors argue that strong cohort data and organic customer acquisition are more reliable evidence of product efficacy than third-party certifications like EWG verification or National Eczema Association acceptance.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: A reusable consumer-diligence heuristic: weight repeat-purchase cohorts above regulatory or certification badges when assessing personal-care brands.
insights.quote: strong cohort data and organic customer acquisition are the best indications that the products just work
insights.locator: Dr. Max’s formulas are EWG verified

insights.claim: The product was validated by demand from over 30,000 patient visits and five years of kitchen prototyping before commercialization, which the investors present as a durable moat built from clinical feedback rather than marketing.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: Founder-embedded distribution (a practicing physician's own patient base) is a repeatable origination pattern worth screening for in consumer health deals.
insights.quote: Born out of organic demand from over 30,000 patient visits, Dr. Max spent 5 years prototyping products in his kitchen before commercializing his modern apothecary.
insights.locator: Born out of organic demand from over 30,000 patient visits

themes.theme: Clean-label consumer demand and exit comps

insights.claim: The natural personal-care exit opportunity is anchored by comparables the investors cite directly: Burt's Bees sold for $925m in 2007, Coterie reportedly sold for over $1b, and Eucerin plus Aquaphor generate roughly €1.5b in annual revenue.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete TAM and exit-value frame for the clean personal-care category; strategics (Clorox-type acquirers and Beiersdorf-scale incumbents) remain the likely liquidity path.
insights.quote: Burt’s Bees (sold for $925m in 2007), Coterie (sold for a reported $1b+) and Eucerin + Aquafor generating €1.5b revenue annually, establish the economic opportunity.
insights.locator: We believe their organic traction is setting the foundation

insights.claim: Parents are increasingly acting as amateur toxicologists — parsing ingredient labels and Yuka scores — creating structural demand for clean-ingredient products that simply work.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: Ingredient-transparency apps are shifting consumer behavior at point of purchase; legacy personal-care incumbents with complex formulations face share loss to clean-label challengers.
insights.quote: In an era where parents are expected to be amateur toxicologists, navigating complicated ingredient labels and judging Yuka scores in their diaper caddies
insights.locator: In an era where parents are expected to be amateur toxicologists

insights.claim: Baby care is one of the highest-consideration purchases for families, so a trusted first product can be expanded into a lifetime family-care platform with unusually high loyalty.
insights.speaker: Amanda Amos & Andrew Montgomery
insights.so_what: The upside case rests on category expansion beyond baby care — watch for line extensions as the proof point that justifies a generational-brand valuation.
insights.quote: In consumer, few are more loyal than a parent who has found the “thing” that finally works.
insights.locator: Baby care is one of the highest consideration purchases
